messages.author: 7fffd6a458b15b54
messages.subject: Run Multiple Rstan Processes
parts:
Hi there,

Would it be ok to run multiple Rstan processes at the same time on a Windows PC? I tried to run several R2Openbugs processes simultaneously and found that the results seem to be very similar, even though the generating values were very different.

Thanks!
Yong

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Run Multiple Rstan Processes
parts:
There shouldn't be a problem doing that.

You should still give the different chains the same
seed and different chain IDs.

I'm not clear on what the best way to save the fit object
in each process then read them all back in to a single process
and combine them into a single fit object for posterior analysis.
But Jiqiang or Ben should know.

- Bob

messages.author: 54e08ddecb38c1b3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Run Multiple Rstan Processes
parts:
You can simple save the chains themselves:

chain1 <-stan(fit=fit1, init =my.inits(), pars=params, data=data.list, warmup = 250, iter=3250, chains = 1, chain_id=1)
save(sample1, file="G:/BackupChris/mallard_spatial_model/chain1.saved")

and then  re-import them in R and combine them into a fit object. 

load("G:/BackupChris/mallard_spatial_model/chain1.saved")
...
model1 <- sflist2stanfit(list(sample1,sample2,sample3, sample4,  sample5,  sample6))
output1<-extract(model1, permuted = TRUE)

Note that if you use that method it will be really important to use the "chain_id" command otherwise some chains could be exact duplicate. 

Finally, I also had problem in the past with BUGS and JAGS so I usually run the chains in different working folders. I never tried to run many chains at the same time with Stan though so you should listen to Bob instead of me. 

Chris
------------------

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Run Multiple Rstan Processes
parts:
On Jul 7, 2014, at 3:52 PM, Christian Roy <christia...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for the response, Christian.

> ...
> Note that if you use that method it will be really important to use the "chain_id" command otherwise some chains could be exact duplicate.

W.r.t. listening to me, the above was the only point I was trying
to make --- if you use the exact same seed in different processes
you'll get the same result. And if you use the default one based
on time, they're likely to be the same seed because the processes
spin up pretty quickly these days and we're not using super fine
grained time-based seeds.

- Bob
